title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The court opens; Colada and Tizón are handed back (tirada 137, lines 3127–3198)
part: Tirada 137 (second part) · The court opens; Colada and Tizón are handed back (lines 3127–3198)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 321–325, lines 3127–3198 (tiradas 137–137). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Essora se levó en pie el buen rey don Alfons;
“Oíd, mesnadas, sí vos vala el Criador!
sentences.l:
Then himself raised on foot the good king don Alfons;
“Hear, household-troops, so you may-help the Creator!
sentences.i: Then the good King Alfonso rose to his feet: “Hear me, my men, so may the Creator help you!
sentences.n: Tirada 137 continues (assonance ó: Alfons, Criador, cortes, Carrión …). Pidal's rubric for this section: the king opens the session and proclaims peace between the parties; the Çid sets out his demand and claims Colada and Tizón; the men of Carrión hand over the swords; the Çid gives them to Pedro Vermúdez and Martín Antolínez (Pidal: El rey abre la sesión. Proclama la paz entre los litigantes.—El Cid expone su demanda. Reclama Colada y Tizón. Los de Carrión entregan las espadas. El Cid las da a Pedro, Vermúdez y Martín Antolínez; the comma after Pedro is a slip of the print: one man, Pedro Vermúdez). Pidal begins v. 3127 with a paragraph indent: the court, now seated (end of the last part), is called to order. Essora, 'then'. se levó en pie, 'rose to his feet': levó is the preterite of levar, 'to raise', here reflexive, levarse en pie = levantarse. el buen rey don Alfons, 'the good King Alfonso' (Alfons, the short form, as throughout). Oíd, 'hear!' (imperative plural of oír). mesnadas, 'household-troops' (house): the king addresses the whole gathering as his men. sí vos vala el Criador, 'so may the Creator help you' (house): sí, 'so, thus', in a wish; vala, present subjunctive of valer, 'help'; vos, 'you', the object.

sentences.t:
Yo, de que fu rey, non fiz mas de dos cortes:
la una f[o] en Burgos, e la otra en Carrión,
esta terçera a Toledo la vin fer oy,
sentences.l:
I, since that I-was king, not I-made more than two courts:
the one was in Burgos, and the other in Carrión,
this third at Toledo it I-came to-make today,
sentences.i: Since I became king I have held no more than two courts: the one was at Burgos and the other at Carrión; this third I have come to hold today at Toledo,
sentences.n: de que fu rey, 'since I was (became) king' (de que, 'since, from the time that'; fu = fui). non fiz mas de dos cortes, 'I did not hold more than two courts' (fiz = hice, from fazer, f- for h-; cortes, 'courts', solemn sittings of the king with his great men). Pidal's note to v. 3130: 'El juglar parece referirse solo a cortes judiciales. Alfonso VI había celebrado corte en Toledo y otros puntos con diferentes motivos. Estos versos del Cantar se perpetuaron, a través de Refundiciones, en la memoria del pueblo y se cantaban asi en el siglo XVI y siguientes: Tres cortes armara el rey, todas tres a una sazón, / las unas armara en Burgos, las otras armó en León, / las otras armó en Toledo, donde los hidalgos son, / para cumplir de justicia al chico con el mayor. Nótese que también este romance se refiere a cortes judiciales' — 'The minstrel seems to mean only courts of justice. Alfonso VI had held court at Toledo and elsewhere for different reasons. These lines of the Cantar lived on, through later reworkings, in the people's memory, and were sung thus in the sixteenth century and after: "Three courts the king assembled, all three at one season; the first he assembled in Burgos, the next he assembled in León, the last in Toledo, where the nobles are, to do justice to the small as to the great." Note that this ballad too means courts of justice.' f[o] = fue, 'was', the o Pidal's restoration. esta terçera … la vin fer oy, 'this third one I have come to hold today': the object said twice (esta terçera … la); vin = vine, 'I came'; fer = hacer, 'to make, hold'. a Toledo, 'at Toledo' (a of place).

sentences.t:
por el amor de mio Çid el que en buen ora naçió,
que reçiba derecho de ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
for the love of my Çid he who in good hour was-born,
that he-may-receive right from infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: for the favour I bear my Çid, who was born in a good hour, so that he may have justice of the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: por el amor de mio Çid, 'for the love of my Çid, for his sake': the king's amor to his vassal, 'favour' (house). el que en buen ora naçió, the formula, 'he who was born in a good hour' (house: 'born in a good hour'). que reçiba derecho de, 'that he may receive right from': reçiba, present subjunctive of reçebir; derecho, 'right, justice' (aver derecho de, 'have justice of', house). ifantes de Carrión, without the article, as usual in the poem.

sentences.i: Great wrong has been done him; we all know it. Let Count Enrique and Count Remond be judges in this, and you other counts who are not of their faction.
sentences.n: Grande tuerto … le han tenido, 'they have done him great wrong' (tener tuerto a uno, 'to wrong someone'; tuerto, 'wrong, injury', the opposite of derecho, 'right'). The comma after tuerto is in the packet; on the scan (seen at zoom 4) the mark after tuerto sits low and close to the word, smaller than the comma after tenido: it may be a stray mark of the print rather than a comma; either way it does not change the sense, and it is passed over in the translations. sabémoslo todos nós, 'we all know it' (sabemos + lo; nós with the accent, the stressed pronoun). alcaldes, 'judges'. Pidal's note to v. 3135: 'alcaldes, voz árabe, sinónima de la latina "jueces". Los alcaldes de la corte debian ser ricos hombres y eran generalmente condes. Por eso aquí el rey nombra jueces a todos los condes, sin más distinción que excluir a los que pertenecen al bando de los de Carrión (3136). El conde don Ramón, como yerno principal del rey (don Anric estaba casado con la hija bastarda del monarca), es el que lleva la voz de los alcaldes, 3208, 3237' — 'alcaldes, an Arabic word, the same as the Latin "judges". The judges of the court had to be great nobles and were generally counts. So here the king names all the counts as judges, with no distinction except to exclude those who belong to the faction of the men of Carrión (3136). Count Ramón, as the king's principal son-in-law (Don Enrique was married to the king's natural daughter), is the one who speaks for the judges, 3208, 3237.' sean desto, 'let them be (judges) of this' (sean, subjunctive of command; desto = de esto). co[m]de don Anrric e co[m]de don Remond, 'Count Enrique and Count Remond' (house); the m of co[m]de is Pidal's restoration. que del vando non sodes, 'who are not of the faction': the king turns from speaking of the counts to speaking to them (sodes = sois, 'you are'); vando = bando, 'faction, party', that of Carrión.

sentences.t:
Todos meted i mientes, ca sodes coñoscedores,
por escoger el derecho, ca tuerto non mando yo.
Della e della part en paz seamos oy.
sentences.l:
All put there minds, for you-are discerning-men,
for to-choose the right, for wrong not command I.
Of-this and of-that side in peace let-us-be today.
sentences.i: Give all your minds to it, for you are men of judgment, to find out the right, for I will have no wrong done. On this side and on that, let us be at peace today.
sentences.n: meted i mientes, 'put your minds to it' (meter mientes, 'to pay heed'; i, 'there, to it'; meted, imperative plural). ca, 'for'. coñoscedores: Pidal's note to v. 3137: 'coñoscedores, "entendidos"' — 'knowledgeable, discerning' (house: 'prudent, discerning'). Pidal's note to v. 3138: '"para hallar el derecho, que yo no mando injusticia"' — 'to find the right, for I do not command injustice'. escoger, literally 'to choose, pick out'. tuerto non mando yo, 'wrong I do not order', i.e. I will have no injustice done. Della e della part: Pidal's note to v. 3139: '"De una y otra parte", v. 1965' — 'on the one side and the other' (della = de la, 'of this … of that', with part, the apocopated parte). en paz seamos oy, 'let us be at peace today' (seamos, subjunctive): no violence in the court.

sentences.t:
Juro par sant Esidr[e], el que bolviere mi cort
quitar me a el reyno, perderá mi amor.
Con el que toviere derecho yo dessa parte me so.
sentences.l:
I-swear by saint Isidore, he who should-disturb my court
quit for-me will the kingdom, he-shall-lose my favour.
With him who should-have right I of-that side myself am.
sentences.i: I swear by Saint Isidore, whoever throws my court into disorder shall leave my kingdom and lose my favour. Whoever has the right on his side, on that side I stand.
sentences.n: Juro par sant Esidr[e], 'I swear by Saint Isidore' (house; par, 'by', in an oath; the final e Pidal's restoration), the king's usual oath. el que bolviere mi cort, 'he who disturbs my court': bolviere, future subjunctive of bolver (= volver), here 'to turn over, throw into confusion' (our reading of the verb in this place: to start a brawl in the sitting court). quitar me a el reyno, a split future: quitar + me + a (= ha), that is me quitará, 'he will quit the kingdom on me', 'will leave my kingdom', banishment; quitar, 'to leave, give up'; the me, the king's, 'my'. perderá mi amor, 'he shall lose my favour' (house: a lord's amor). Con el que toviere derecho, 'with him who has right' (toviere, future subjunctive of tener). yo dessa parte me so, 'I am on that side' (dessa = de essa; so = soy; me, the reflexive pronoun the old language often sets beside ser, adding nothing to the sense).

sentences.t:
Agora demande mio Çid el Campeador:
sabremos qué responden ifantes de Carrión.”
sentences.l:
Now let-demand my Çid the Campeador:
we-shall-know what answer infantes of Carrión.”
sentences.i: Now let my Çid the Campeador make his claim; we shall hear what the Infantes of Carrión answer.”
sentences.n: demande, 'let him demand, make his claim' (present subjunctive of demandar, a term of the court: demanda, 'claim, suit'). sabremos, 'we shall know' (future of saber). qué responden, 'what they answer' (present, as now). The king's speech ends here.

sentences.t:
Mio Çid la mano besó al rey e en pie se levantó:
“Mucho vos lo gradesco como a rey e a señor,
por quanto esta cort fiziestes por mi amor.
sentences.l:
My Çid the hand kissed to-the king and on foot himself raised:
“Much to-you it I-thank as to king and to lord,
for as-much-as this court you-made for my love.
sentences.i: My Çid kissed the king's hand and rose to his feet: “I thank you greatly for it, as my king and my lord, for having held this court out of love for me.
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3145 with a paragraph indent. la mano besó al rey, 'kissed the hand to the king', i.e. the king's hand (the person in the dative). e en pie se levantó, 'and rose to his feet' (levantarse, as now). Pidal's note to v. 3145: 'Los litigantes debian estar de pie para hacer sus alegaciones' — 'The parties had to be on their feet to make their pleas.' Mucho vos lo gradesco, 'I thank you much for it' (gradesco = agradezco). como a rey e a señor, 'as (one thanks) a king and lord'. por quanto, 'inasmuch as, for the fact that'. fiziestes = hicisteis, 'you made, held' (f- for h-; old -stes ending). por mi amor, 'for love of me, for my sake'.

sentences.i: This is what I demand of the Infantes of Carrión. For my daughters whom they abandoned I bear no dishonour, for it was you who married them, O king; you will know what to do today.
sentences.n: Esto les demando a ifantes de Carrión, 'this I demand of them, of the Infantes', the person said twice (les … a). por mis fijas quem dexaron, 'for my daughters whom they left (on me)': quem = que me, the me a dative of the person affected; dexaron, 'they left, abandoned' (dexar = dejar). yo non he desonor, 'I have no dishonour' (he, 'I have', aver; desonor, 'dishonour', house). ca vos las casastes, rey, 'for you married them, king': the dishonour of the marriage falls on the king who made it, as the Çid said when he sent Muño Gustioz to him (vv. 2908–2911, tiradas 132–133). sabredes qué fer oy, 'you will know what to do today' (sabredes = sabréis; fer = hacer). The Çid leaves the dishonour to the king and does not sue for it now: the Infantes take note of this (v. 3165).

sentences.t:
mas quando sacaron mis fijas de Valençia la mayor,
yo bien l[o]s quería d' alma e de coraçón.
sentences.l:
but when they-took my daughters from Valençia the great,
I well them loved from soul and from heart.
sentences.i: But when they took my daughters away from Valencia the great, I loved them well, with all my soul and heart.
sentences.n: mas, 'but'. sacaron … de Valençia la mayor, 'they took out from Valencia the great' (Valençia kept so in the literal line, 'Valencia' in the English, house). yo bien l[o]s quería, 'I loved them well': los, the Infantes; the o is Pidal's restoration (the masculine, for the sons-in-law). d' alma e de coraçón, 'with soul and with heart' (d' for de before a vowel). The sentence ends with a full stop in Pidal, and the next line begins with small diles: the sense runs on.

sentences.i: I gave them two swords, Colada and Tizón — these I won like a man — that they might do themselves honour with them and serve you;
sentences.n: diles = di + les, 'I gave them' (dar, preterite). a Colada e a Tizón, the personal a before the swords' names, as at v. 2575 (darvos he dos espadas, a Colada e a Tizón): the swords are named like persons. Colada the Çid won from the Count of Barcelona at Tévar (tiradas 56–59; he says so at v. 3195); Tizón from King Búcar (tiradas 118–119); Tizón 'Tizón' (house). estas yo las gané, 'these I won', the object twice; between dashes in Pidal, an aside. a guisa de varón, 'in the manner of a man', 'like a man' (guisa, 'manner'), as at v. 2576. ques ondrassen = que se ondrassen, 'that they might honour themselves', imperfect subjunctive of ondrar (= honrar), the se cut to s and glued to que. sirviessen a vos, 'might serve you' (servir).

sentences.i: since they abandoned my daughters in the oak-wood of Corpes, they would have nothing to do with me, and they lost my favour: let them give me back my swords, since they are my sons-in-law no longer.”
sentences.n: quando, 'when', and here with the sense 'since, now that' (so also in v. 3158). robredo, 'oak-wood' (house), the robredo de Corpes of the outrage (tiradas 128–130). comigo non quisieron aver nada, 'with me they would have nothing' (comigo = conmigo; quisieron, preterite of querer; aver, 'to have'). perdieron mi amor, 'they lost my favour' (house: the amor of the man above to those below him; the Çid was their father-in-law and lord of their household). denme, 'let them give me' (present subjunctive dar + me). mios yernos, 'my sons-in-law'. Pidal's note to v. 3158: 'El cambio de armas era señal de parentesco y amistad, 2093. El Cid, no sólo había dado estas dos espadas a los infantes, sino otras dos anteriormente' — 'The exchange of arms was a sign of kinship and friendship, 2093. The Cid had given the Infantes not only these two swords but two others before.' Since the kinship is broken, the swords come back.

sentences.t:
Atorgan los alcaldes: “tod esto es razón.”
Dixo co[m]de don Garçía: “a esto fablemos nos.”
sentences.l:
Grant the judges: “all this is reason.”
Said count don García: “on this let-speak we.”
sentences.i: The judges grant it: “All this is just.” Count García said: “Let us confer on this.”
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3159 with a paragraph indent. Atorgan, 'they grant, assent' (atorgar = otorgar). tod esto es razón, 'all this is reason', 'all this is right and just' (tod for todo before a vowel; razón, 'what is right, reasonable'). co[m]de don Garçía, 'Count García' (house), the Garci Ordóñez of v. 1345, the Çid's enemy and of the Infantes' party; the m is Pidal's. a esto fablemos nos, 'on this let us speak', 'let us talk this over among ourselves' (fablemos, subjunctive of fablar, f- for h-; nos, 'we', the subject, at the end).

sentences.i: Then the Infantes of Carrión went out apart, with all their kinsmen and the faction that was there with them; quickly they talked it over and agreed on their answer:
sentences.n: salién, 'they were going out' (imperfect of salir, -ién for -ían). aparte, 'apart, aside'. s[o]s = sus, 'their', the o Pidal's restoration. y el bando, 'and the faction' (y for e here, as printed; bando, the vando of v. 3136). que í son, 'who are there' (í = allí). Pidal's note to v. 3163: '"aprisa lo iban tratando y convienen la respuesta". Acceden muy fácilmente, pues, como cobardes, no estiman las espadas que después les infundirán espanto (3643, 3665). Este adverbio apriessa contrasta con las graves dificultades que hallan después los infantes para responder a la otra demanda del Cid, la del dinero, y con las quejas en que prorrumpen, v. 3218, 3207' — '"quickly they were discussing it and agree on the answer". They give way very easily, for, being cowards, they set no value on the swords, which will later fill them with terror (3643, 3665). This adverb apriessa contrasts with the grave difficulties the Infantes meet later in answering the Cid's other demand, the one for the money, and with the complaints they break into, v. 3218, 3207.' ivan trayendo, 'were treating, handling' (traer in Pidal's sense 'tratar'; ir + gerund). acuerdan la razón, 'they agree the answer' (acordar, 'agree upon'; razón here 'what is to be said'). The tenses shift from imperfect to present.

sentences.i: “The Çid Campeador does us a great favour still, since he does not sue us today for the dishonour of his daughters; we shall easily come to terms with King Alfonso.
sentences.n: Aun, 'still, even so'. grand amor nos faze: Pidal's note to v. 3164: 'grand amor, "gran favor"' — 'a great favour'. faze = hace (f- for h-). quando, 'since'. desondra de sus fijas, 'the dishonour of his daughters', what was done to them (desondra, like desonor, 'dishonour', house). no nos demanda oy, 'he does not demand of us today', the suit he has left to the king (v. 3150). bien nos abendremos, 'we shall come to terms well, easily' (abendremos, future of abenir = avenir, 'agree', with the d of the old future as in vendremos).

sentences.i: Let us give him his swords, since his claim ends there; and when he has them, the court will break up; the Çid Campeador will have no more right against us.”
sentences.n: Démosle, 'let us give him' (demos + le). Pidal's note to v. 3167: 'finca la boz, "acaba la demanda"; comp. 3211' — 'the claim ends; compare 3211' (where the Infantes say so to the court, in the next part). quando, 'since'. finca, 'remains, stays', here 'stops' (fincar, f-); boz = voz, 'voice', in the court 'claim, plea'. quando las toviere, 'when he has them' (toviere, future subjunctive of tener). partir se a la cort, split future: partir + se + a (= ha), that is se partirá, 'the court will break up, disperse'. ya mas non avrá derecho de nos, 'no more will he have right from us': nothing more can be claimed (avrá, future of aver; de nos, 'from us'). Canpeador, with n before p, as printed here.

sentences.i: With this agreed between them they went back into the court: “Mercy, O King Alfonso! You are our lord. We cannot deny it: he gave us two swords;
sentences.n: aquesta = esta, 'this'. fabla, 'talk, speech' (= habla, f- for h-), what they had agreed among themselves. tornaron, 'they returned'. Merçed, ya rey don Alfons, 'Mercy, O King Alfonso' (house: Merçed heading a petition, 'Mercy, O king'; ya, the old vocative 'O'). sodes nuestro señor, 'you are our lord' (sodes = sois). No lo podemos negar, 'we cannot deny it'. ca, 'for'. nos dió, 'he gave us', the Çid, not named.

sentences.t:
quando las demanda e dellas ha sabor,
dárgelas queremos delant estando vos.”
sentences.l:
since them he-demands and of-them he-has desire,
to-give-to-him-them we-wish before being you.”
sentences.i: since he asks for them and longs to have them, we are willing to give them to him here in your presence.”
sentences.n: quando, 'since'. Pidal's note to v. 3173: 'dellas ha sabor, "las desea"' — 'he desires them' (aver sabor de, 'to have a liking, a desire for'; dellas = de ellas). dárgelas, 'to give them to him': dar + ge (the old form of le before lo, la: modern se) + las (dárselas). queremos, 'we wish, are willing'. delant estando vos, 'you being present before (us)', 'in your presence' (delant = delante; estando vos, the gerund with its own subject).

sentences.t:
Sacaron las espadas Colada e Tizón,
pusiéronlas en mano del rey so señor:
sentences.l:
They-drew-out the swords Colada and Tizón,
put-them in hand of-the king their lord:
sentences.i: They brought out the swords Colada and Tizón and put them into the hand of the king their lord.
sentences.n: Pidal begins v. 3175 with a paragraph indent. Sacaron, 'they brought out' (sacar). las espadas Colada e Tizón, here without the personal a. pusiéronlas, 'they put them' (pusieron + las). en mano del rey so señor, 'in the hand of the king their lord' (so = su).

sentences.i: They draw the swords, and the whole court gleams; the pommels and the guards are all of gold; the worthy men of the court marvel at them.
sentences.n: saca[n] las espadas, 'they draw the swords' (from the scabbards), the n Pidal's restoration (the plural; the subject, 'they', is not named); the present after the preterites of v. 3175–76. relumbra toda la cort, 'the whole court gleams, shines' (relumbrar). Pidal's note to v. 3178: 'maçana, "pomo"; arriaz, "gavilán"' — 'maçana, the pommel; arriaz, the quillon, the cross-guard' (maçana is literally 'apple', from the shape of the knob at the end of the hilt). todos d' oro son, 'all are of gold'. maravíllanse dellas, 'they marvel at them' (maravillarse de). los omnes buenos de la cort, 'the good men of the court', the worthy men, the nobles present (omnes = hombres).

sentences.i: The king called my Çid and gave him the swords; he received the swords and kissed his hands, and went back to the bench from which he had risen.
sentences.n: Line 3179b is wholly in Pidal's italic: the whole verse is his restoration, printed plain here; Pidal gives it no number, and the letter b is ours (after 3179), as the edition does with unnumbered restored lines. It supplies the step the manuscript leaves out, the swords passing from the king to the Çid; Pidal gives no footnote on it. llamó, 'called' (llamar), with a mio Çid, the personal a. las espadas le dio, 'he gave him the swords'. reçibió, 'he received'. las manos le besó, 'he kissed his hands', the king's. tornos = tornó + se, 'he went back'. al escaño, 'to the bench' (house), the bench of turned wood on which he had sat (v. 3121). don[t] se levantó, 'whence he had risen' (dont, 'whence, from where', Latin de unde; the t is Pidal's restoration).

sentences.t:
En las manos las tiene e amas las cató;
non l[as] pueden camear, ca el Çid bien las connosçe;
sentences.l:
In the hands them he-holds and both them he-looked-at;
not them they-can change, for the Çid well them knows;
sentences.i: He holds them in his hands and looks at them both; no one can change them for others, for the Çid knows them well.
sentences.n: En las manos las tiene, 'in his hands he holds them' (the object twice: espadas understood, las). amas las cató, 'he looked at them both' (amas = ambas; cató, preterite of catar, 'look at'); present tiene, then preterite cató, the tense-mixing. non l[as] pueden camear, 'they cannot change them': camear = cambiar, 'to exchange' (as camearon at v. 2093, where the Infantes and the Çid exchanged swords), here 'swap, put others in their place'; pueden has no stated subject, 'they, anyone'. The as of las is Pidal's restoration. On the scan the m of camear is damaged (it looks like ın, 'caınear'); camear is the word, a reading on the damaged letter. ca el Çid bien las connosçe, 'for the Çid knows them well' (connosçe = conoce).

sentences.t:
alegrósle tod el cuerpo, sonrrisós de coraçón,
alçava la mano, a la barba se tomó;
sentences.l:
rejoiced-itself-to-him all the body, smiled-himself from heart,
he-was-raising the hand, to the beard himself he-took;
sentences.i: His whole body was filled with gladness; he smiled from his heart; he raised his hand and took hold of his beard:
sentences.n: alegrósle tod el cuerpo, 'all his body rejoiced in him' (alegró + se + le; tod for todo before a vowel). sonrrisós, 'he smiled' (sonrrisó + se, the se cut to s: preterite of sonrrisar = sonreír, a regular -ar verb). de coraçón, 'from the heart'. alçava la mano, 'he was raising his hand' (imperfect among preterites). a la barba se tomó, 'took hold of his beard' (tomarse a, 'to seize'), the gesture that comes before his oaths, as at vv. 2476 and 2829.

sentences.t:
“par aquesta barba que nadi non messó,
assís irán vengando don Elvira e doña Sol.”
sentences.l:
“by this beard which nobody not plucked,
thus-themselves shall-go avenging don Elvira and doña Sol.”
sentences.i: “By this beard, which no one has ever plucked, so shall Doña Elvira and Doña Sol go on being avenged.”
sentences.n: par, 'by', in an oath. aquesta = esta. nadi … non, 'no one … not', the double negative (nadi = nadie, as at v. 2832; the scan has a broken mark under the n, read as nadi). messó, preterite of messar, 'to pluck (hair)': to pull a man's beard was the gravest insult, and the Çid's has never suffered it. assís = assí + se, 'thus (themselves)'. irán vengando, 'they will go on being avenged': ir + gerund, the action going on, the se making it passive, 'so shall they be avenged, step by step' — the swords are the first part of the reparation. don Elvira e doña Sol: don before Elvira as printed, 'Doña Elvira' in the English (house).

sentences.i: He called his nephew Don Pero by his name, stretched out his arm and gave him the sword Tizón: “Take it, nephew, for it has gained a better lord.”
sentences.n: A so sobrino … llamó, 'he called his nephew' (so = su). [don Pero]: the two words are Pidal's restoration. Don Pero is Per Vermudoz (house: 'Don Pero' as at v. 2340, the same man): Pidal's rubric names him, 'Pedro Vermúdez', and the Çid calls Per Vermudoz his nephew at v. 2351 (el mio sobrino caro). por nómbrel llamó, 'he called him by his name' (nómbrel = nombre + le, the le cut to l and glued on). tendió el braço, 'he stretched out his arm' (tender; braço = brazo). la espada Tizón le dió, 'gave him the sword Tizón' (house: Tizón). Prendetla = prended + la, 'take it' (imperative plural of respect; d before l written t). ca mejora en señor, 'for it betters in lord': the sword gains by changing masters, it goes to a better lord than the one it had (the Infantes); our reading of the phrase, which is short and proverbial.

sentences.t:
A Martín Antolínez, el Burgalés de pro,
tendió el braço, el espada Coládal dio;
sentences.l:
To Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese of worth,
he-stretched the arm, the sword Colada-to-him he-gave;
sentences.i: To Martín Antolínez, the worthy man of Burgos, he stretched out his arm and gave him the sword Colada:
sentences.n: el Burgalés de pro, 'the worthy man of Burgos' (house; de pro, 'of worth'). tendió el braço, as in v. 3189. el espada, 'the sword' (el, the old feminine article before a vowel, beside la espada in v. 3189). Coládal = Colada + le, 'gave him Colada', the le cut to l and glued to the name (the accent marks the stress, Coláda-l).

sentences.t:
“Martín Antolínez, mio vassallo de pro,
prended a Colada, ganéla de buen señor,
de Remont Verenguel de Barçilona la mayor.
sentences.l:
“Martín Antolínez, my vassal of worth,
take to Colada, I-won-it from good lord,
from Remont Verenguel of Barçilona the great.
sentences.i: “Martín Antolínez, my worthy vassal, take Colada: I won it from a good lord, from Remont Verenguel of Barcelona the great.
sentences.n: mio vassallo de pro, 'my vassal of worth'. prended a Colada, 'take Colada' (prended, imperative plural of respect; the personal a before the sword's name). Pidal opens v. 3194 with an opening quotation mark instead of the closing one he uses at the start of each line of a speech: a slip of the print; the repeated line-initial quotes are dropped in this edition, so the text is not affected. ganéla, 'I won it' (gané + la). de buen señor, 'from a good lord'. Remont Verenguel, the Count of Barcelona (Ramón Berenguer), from whom the Çid won Colada in the pine-wood of Tévar (tiradas 56–59); the name kept as printed, as there. Barçilona la mayor, 'Barcelona the great', the same epithet as Valençia la mayor.

sentences.t:
Por esso vos la do que la bien curiedes vos.
Sé que si vos acaeçiere [o viniere sazón],
con ella ganaredes grand prez e grand valor.”
sentences.l:
For that to-you it I-give that it well you-may-guard you.
I-know that if to-you it-should-befall [or should-come occasion],
with it you-will-win great renown and great worth.”
sentences.i: I give it to you for this, that you may guard it well. I know that if the chance befalls you, or the time comes, with it you will win great renown and great worth.”
sentences.n: Pidal's note to v. 3196: 'Literalmente, "os la doy para que la cuidéis bien' (the closing quote mark is missing in the print) — 'Literally, "I give it to you so that you may take good care of it".' do = doy, 'I give'. curiedes, present subjunctive of curiar, 'to take care of, guard' (= curéis); vos, 'you', said again at the end. Sé que, 'I know that'. si vos acaeçiere, 'if it befall you' (acaeçiere, future subjunctive of acaeçer, 'to happen'; the thing that befalls not named: a battle, a need). [o viniere sazón], 'or the time come': the whole half-line is Pidal's restoration, in his italic, and he gives no note; sazón, 'time, occasion' (viniere, future subjunctive of venir). The line 3197b, numbered so by Pidal, completes the sentence. ganaredes, 'you will win' (= ganaréis). grand prez e grand valor, 'great renown and great worth' (prez, 'honour, renown'; valor, 'worth, merit').

sentences.t: Besóle la mano, el espada reçibió.
sentences.l: Kissed-him the hand, the sword he-received.
sentences.i: Martín Antolínez kissed his hand and received the sword.
sentences.n: Besóle la mano, 'he kissed his hand' (besó + le). The subject, Martín Antolínez, is not named. el espada, as in v. 3192. reçibió, 'received'. The part ends here; tirada 137 runs on (to v. 3249), with the Çid rising again to make his second demand, for the money he gave the Infantes, in the next part.
